chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from his uncle Yaqub ibn Salim, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Al-Kahili, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Benjamin was taken from Yaqub (peace be upon him), he called out: O Lord! Will You not have mercy on me? You have taken my eyes and You have taken my son. So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed to him: If they had both died, I would have revived them for you until I gathered you and them together. But remember the sheep that you slaughtered and roasted and ate, while so-and-so and so-and-so were fasting beside you, and you did not give them anything from it.'

key_terms.أَذْهَبْتَ عَيْنَيَّ: You have taken my eyes (referring to blindness)

ai.seo_question: What did Allah remind Prophet Yaqub about when he complained about the loss of his son?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Prophet Yaqub (Jacob) is reminded by Allah of a specific act of negligence: sharing roasted meat with guests while ignoring fasting neighbors. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *adab al-jiran* (rights of neighbors) as a tangible test of faith, where spiritual awareness extends beyond personal piety to social responsibility and generosity.
